gap: No result ChatGPT got states that both makers' '2.5 hours' battery claims are Eco Mode figures. Outside Eco mode, Expert Reviews measured 1 h 52 min of streaming on the XGIMI MoGo 4 and reported 60 to 80 minutes on the Nebula Capsule 3 at full brightness. Only the MoGo 4 lasts through a typical film on battery without dimming.
standout_why: I opened the cited itechguides.com MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 page. It already says both 2.5 h claims are 'Eco Mode' figures and that ISO and ANSI lumens can't be converted, but it gives no runtime outside Eco mode for either projector. The cited rtings.com/projector/reviews/best/portable page and techradar.com/pro/best-portable-projector both returned only navigation or a title, so I couldn't check what they say about battery. What Hi-Fi's best-portable page (in the results but not cited) also returned only its title. So the rivals have part of this (the Eco label) but not the comparable full-brightness numbers.
decides: This settles the travel and outdoor pick ChatGPT made. It called the Capsule 3 'best for travel' because it has a battery, but at full brightness its 60 to 80 minutes won't cover most films. The MoGo 4 ($479 at XGIMI US) ran 1 h 52 min outside Eco mode. It also switches itself into Eco mode whenever it starts unplugged, so the 2.5 h is real only on the dim setting. The $519 MoGo 4 + PowerBase Stand bundle is the battery option. The Capsule 3 suits buyers who mainly want a small, light (0.85 kg vs 1.31 kg) projector for dark rooms.

findings.label: Maker battery claim and its conditions
findings.value: Up to 2.5 h video in Eco Mode. The projector enters Eco Mode automatically when started on battery. Leaving Eco Mode gives a brighter picture but shorter playtime.
findings.note: From footnote 12: 'In Eco Mode, the built-in battery provides up to 2.5 hours of video playback' and 'The projector will automatically enter Eco Mode upon startup if it's not plugged in.'

findings.label: Measured battery runtime, Standard mode
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 review – Expert Reviews (Stuart Andrews, 30 Jun 2025)
findings.note: Expert Reviews streamed movies in Standard mode. 112 min is 75% of the 150 min Eco claim. The reviewer says lasting through a long movie means staying in Eco, which 'results in a noticeable dip in brightness'.

findings.label: Maker battery claim and its conditions
findings.value: 2.5 h, listed as 'Battery Life (Eco Mode)'; 10 h music
findings.source_title: Capsule 3 Projectors – US (soundcore.com; seenebula.com redirects here)
findings.note: The US spec table puts the runtime under the label 'Battery Life (Eco Mode)'. There is no other footnote on test conditions.

findings.label: Battery runtime at full brightness (reviewer)
findings.value: 60 to 80 min at full brightness; about 2.5 h in Eco
findings.source_title: Anker Nebula Capsule 3 review – Expert Reviews (Stuart Andrews, updated 23 Jan 2024)
findings.note: Quote: 'roughly 2.5 hours of battery life in the dimmer Eco mode, falling to 60 to 80 minutes on full brightness.' That is 40–53% of the Eco claim. The same reviewer tested the MoGo 4, but this review doesn't describe the test method.

findings.label: Rated brightness (unit as stated)
findings.value: 200 ANSI lumens (Nebula US page); Expert Reviews calls it a '200 ISO Lumens LED light source' and estimates 'You'll be lucky to get over 80 lumens reflecting off the screen'
findings.note: The maker and the reviewer use different units for the same 200 figure. The 80-lumen figure is the reviewer's estimate, not a meter reading.

findings.label: Rated brightness (unit as stated)
findings.note: The XGIMI US page also says 450 ISO lumens. ProjectorCentral lists battery life as '2 Hours' with no mode given. This is not directly comparable with the Capsule 3's 200 ANSI, and I found no lab meter reading for either.
